body:
Summary- Add voiceprint candidate storage and lifecycle speaker embeddings captured while session exists be bound to names later.
- Extract speaker-specific voiceprint candidates from session audio using anlg-voiceprint + WeSpeaker ONNX, store vectors in OS keyring, and insert rows.
- Add ops to list, promote candidate voiceprint_exemplars (moving keyring first), and tombstone/purge expired candidates and theirring refs.
- Wire extraction/promotion/expiry in the desktop: extraction runs after transcripts persist (gated by new remember_speakers setting), promotion happens a is/reassigned, and periodic sweep removes expired candidates.
- Add a Remember speakers toggle (default off in Audio settings; unnamed expire after45 days.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches local biometric-style embeddings, keyring secrets, and new DB lifecycle around speaker labeling; data stays on-device but mishandling could affect privacy or speaker attribution.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **on-device speaker memory**: when **Remember speakers** is enabled (new Audio setting, default off), the app builds local voiceprints from meeting audio so named transcript speakers can be recognized later.
> 
> A new **`voiceprint`** crate picks clean single-speaker spans from transcript words; **`tauri-plugin-transcription`** embeds those clips with WeSpeaker ONNX, stores vectors in the **OS keyring**, and records metadata in new SQLite tables (`voiceprint_candidates` with 45-day expiry, `voiceprint_exemplars` after promotion). Tauri commands **extract** candidates after transcripts are saved, **promote** them when a speaker is linked to a contact, and **sweep** expired unnamed candidates.
> 
> The desktop passes `remember_speakers` through batch/capture lifecycle and exposes copy in **General → Audio** (plus i18n catalog updates).
>

title: feat(desktop): remember speakers via on-device voiceprints
